name: Petrified Current
classification: Persistent Geometric Paradox / Class-VII Spatial Fracture

detectability.signature: Massive spatial metric distortion with gravitational lensing artifacts and intermittent tachyon bursts

proximity: Navigation computers produce contradictory position readings, reporting the ship at multiple coordinates simultaneously
Visual observation reveals impossible geometry: parallel lines converging, objects appearing to recede and approach at the same time
contact: Internal ship dimensions become inconsistent; corridors measure differently depending on direction of travel
Light follows curved paths inside the zone, creating persistent visual distortions and false horizons
Communication signals loop back on themselves, arriving before they are sent
prolonged_exposure: Ship structural integrity threatened as hull geometry subtly warps to conform to local spatial rules
Crew experience severe spatial disorientation, inability to judge distance or direction, and persistent vertigo
Risk of permanent spatial displacement if the zone undergoes a metric shift while a vessel is inside

age: Unknown; the zone's temporal properties make dating unreliable, though surrounding stellar drift suggests at least 50,000 years

behavior.cycle: Irregular metric shifts occurring every 3 to 19 days, during which the zone's internal geometry reconfigures

phenomena: Ships inside the zone can observe their own stern from the bridge viewport, as light paths curve back on themselves
Physical objects thrown in a straight line return to the thrower from a different direction
The zone contains frozen wavefronts: visible ripples of light suspended in space like the surface of a flash-petrified river
During metric shifts, the zone briefly becomes navigable before snapping into a new impossible configuration
hazards: Metric shifts can trap or displace vessels into geometrically isolated pockets with no viable exit vector
Structural stress on hulls from conflicting spatial geometries, potentially causing breaches in rigid-frame ships
Crew psychological damage from sustained exposure to impossible spatial relationships
opportunities: Study of the zone's geometry could yield breakthroughs in faster-than-light travel theory
During brief navigable windows, the zone functions as a spatial shortcut, compressing enormous distances
Frozen light wavefronts contain encoded information from events that occurred thousands of years ago
known_incidents: The exploration frigate Cardinal Direction entered the zone in 2402 and emerged eleven minutes later from a point 340 light-years away. The crew reported experiencing six days of transit and described internal geometries that their instruments could not record.

A automated probe array launched into the zone in 2455 returned data suggesting the interior volume exceeds the exterior by a factor of several thousand, with some probes still transmitting from locations that should not exist.
description: The Petrified Current appears as a region of space where light itself seems to have solidified mid-flow. Vast luminous ripples hang motionless in the void, frozen wavefronts from ancient stellar events caught in geometries that refuse to resolve. The visual effect is of a river turned to stone at the moment of its greatest turbulence, its currents and eddies preserved in hard light and warped starfield.

Inside the zone, the rules of Euclidean space do not apply. Straight lines curve, parallel paths diverge and reconverge, and distances change depending on the direction of measurement. A ship traveling what its instruments report as a straight course may find itself returned to its starting point, approaching from an unexpected vector. The geometry is not random but follows consistent, if incomprehensible, internal logic that reconfigures itself during unpredictable metric shifts.

The Petrified Current was discovered when a trade route survey detected impossible gravitational lensing patterns in what should have been empty space. Early unmanned probes returned data so contradictory that instrument failure was assumed until multiple independent missions confirmed the readings. The zone has since become one of the most studied and least understood anomalies in charted space, attracting theoretical physicists and daring navigators in roughly equal measure.

Current conditions within the Petrified Current are characterized by increasing metric shift frequency, with intervals between reconfigurations shortening from a historical average of twelve days to as little as three. Whether this represents a natural cycle or a progression toward some critical threshold is a matter of urgent debate. Several research stations maintain position at safe distances, monitoring the zone continuously, while a small but persistent community of navigators attempts to map the brief windows of traversability that each shift creates.
